q: A through consignment is carried over three zonal railways under one through charge, which is collected entirely by the booking railway. The booking railway claims it can retain the entire amount because it collected it. What is the correct position?

options.A: The booking railway retains all, since collection decides ownership
options.B: The destination railway takes all, since it delivers the goods
options.C: The earnings are apportioned among all the railways concerned in proportion to the service rendered, normally the distance carried on each
options.D: The amount is credited wholly to the Railway Board

e: Collection does not decide ownership. Through earnings are apportioned so each railway gets the share it earned, measured normally by distance carried.

q: A passenger travels entirely within one zonal railway, from a station on that railway to another station on the same railway. How are the earnings of this traffic treated?

options.A: The whole earning belongs to that one railway and no apportionment is needed
options.B: The earning is apportioned with the neighbouring railway by distance
options.C: The earning is transferred to Western Railway for division
options.D: The earning is settled in cash as an IRFA transaction

e: This is local traffic - it originates and terminates on the same railway. The whole earning belongs to that railway; only through traffic needs apportionment.

q: Goods are booked at a through rate that includes terminal charges for loading and delivery work done at the two ends. Before dividing the freight among the carrying railways, what is the first step?

options.A: Divide the whole freight by distance, including the terminal charges
options.B: Credit the whole freight to the intermediate railway with the longest lead
options.C: Retain the whole freight with the originating railway
options.D: Take out the terminal charges (and transhipment charges, if any) and credit them to the railways that do that work

e: Terminals come first. Terminal and transhipment charges are deducted from the originating freight before the balance is apportioned on distance.

q: A passenger books luggage on a through journey over two railways and the accounts office proposes to apportion the luggage earnings between the zones by distance. What is the correct treatment?

options.A: Apportion the luggage earnings equally between the two railways
options.B: Luggage earnings are not apportioned between zones; the earning stays where it arises
options.C: Apportion the luggage earnings in proportion to time taken
options.D: Settle the luggage earnings in cash as IRFA

e: Luggage is not apportioned - in the bank's terms the percentage of apportionment for luggage is nil. The passenger-fare distance rule must not be carried over to luggage.

q: A Travelling Ticket Examiner collects excess fare from passengers on a train running over his own railway. How are these TTE earnings treated?

options.A: They are apportioned among all railways on the train's route by distance
options.B: They are credited entirely to the destination railway
options.C: They are retained by the collecting railway and are not put through apportionment
options.D: They are closed to Miscellaneous Government Account

e: Earnings of TTEs are retained by the collecting railway and are not apportioned like ordinary earnings.

q: A passenger travels on a Blank Paper Ticket (BPT) over two railways under a through fare. Is the BPT fare apportioned, and if so, on what basis?

options.A: Yes, a BPT is apportioned in proportion to the kilometres travelled on each railway
options.B: No, a BPT is never apportioned
options.C: Yes, it is apportioned in proportion to the number of stations on each railway
options.D: No, the fare stays wholly with the issuing railway

e: A BPT is apportioned. Through passenger revenue, including BPT, is divided in proportion to the kilometres travelled on each railway.

q: Railway A raises a debit against Railway B through a Transfer Certificate. Railway B examines the claim and does not agree with it. What should Railway B do?

options.A: Pay the amount first and claim a refund later
options.B: Write off the amount on its own authority
options.C: Take the debit to account silently and close the suspense
options.D: Return the Transfer Certificate with its objections; the item remains outstanding until settled

e: A respondent that does not agree returns the Transfer Certificate with objections. The item stays outstanding until the matter is settled.

q: Defence traffic is booked at a station on a credit note / warrant issued by the department, without cash payment at the station. How is this traffic accounted for?

options.A: It is free traffic and no charge is raised
options.B: The charges are taken under Traffic Suspense as demands recoverable, billed on the department and recovered from it
options.C: The charges are written off at the end of the year
options.D: The charges are apportioned as luggage earnings

e: Government traffic on credit notes is not free. The station debit rests under Traffic Suspense and clearance is by raising bills and recovering the amount from the department.

q: At the end of the financial year, a zonal railway still has a balance under Transfer Railways that could not be cleared. To which head is this balance closed?

options.A: To Balance, like all other suspense heads
options.C: To Miscellaneous Government Account / Revenue

e: Transfer Railways is the exception among suspense heads: its year-end balance is closed to Miscellaneous Government Account/Revenue, while other suspense heads close to Balance. The aim remains a nil balance.

q: Two zonal railways decide to settle a prescribed inter-railway claim in cash through financial adjustment, instead of through a book transfer transaction. Such a transaction is known as what?

options.A: An IRFA transaction - Inter-Railway Financial Adjustment
options.C: An intra-railway transfer

e: Transactions between two railways settled in cash by financial adjustment, instead of through transfer transactions in accounts, are IRFA transactions. Book adjustments are not IRFA.

q:
Consider the following statements about the three bases of earnings:
1. The operating ratio is calculated on apportioned earnings.
2. The station Balance Sheet reflects collected revenue.
3. At the all-India level, earnings are reckoned on the originating basis.
4. Advance statements of gross earnings are prepared on apportioned earnings.
Which of the above statements are correct?

options.A: 1, 2 and 4 only
options.C: 1 and 3 only

e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: advance statements of gross earnings are prepared on originating earnings, not apportioned earnings.

q:
Consider the following statements about centralised apportionment:
1. Apportionment of earnings is centralised and is not done independently by each zonal railway.
2. It is carried out on the distance basis through the computerised system of CRIS.
3. Western Railway is the nodal railway that co-ordinates apportionment of earnings.
4. The net results of apportionment appear in Part A of the Traffic Book.
Which of the above statements are correct?

options.C: 2 and 4 only

e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: net results of apportionment appear in Part B of the Traffic Book; Part A deals with station accounts.

q:
Consider the following statements about IRFA:
1. No IRFA is done on account of pilgrim / terminal tax.
2. No IRFA is done on account of printed card tickets.
3. No IRFA is done on account of reservation charges.
4. IRFA transactions are settled by book debit and credit through Transfer Railways.
Which of the above statements are correct?

options.A: 1 and 2 only
options.C: 1, 2 and 3 only

e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 list the bank-keyed exclusions from IRFA. Statement 4 is wrong: IRFA is cash settlement; book adjustment through Transfer Railways is a transfer transaction, not IRFA.

q:
Consider the following statements about terminal and line-haul components:
1. Terminal expenses are not affected by the lead (distance) of the traffic.
2. Line-haul expenses grow broadly with distance and load carried.
3. Terminal charges are credited to the railways that do the end-work.
4. Terminal charges are apportioned among all intermediate railways by distance.
Which of the above statements are correct?

options.A: 1, 2 and 3 only
options.C: 2 and 4 only

e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: terminal charges are taken out before apportionment and settled with the terminal railways, not spread by distance.

q: Which part of the Traffic Book carries the net results of apportionment of traffic earnings?

options.A: Part A
options.C: Part D

e: Part B of the Traffic Book carries the net results of apportionment. Part A deals with station accounts and Part C carries the Traffic Account proper.

q: NTKM (Net Tonne Kilometres) measures which of the following?

options.A: Gross load including tare weight multiplied by distance
options.B: Paying (net) load of goods traffic multiplied by distance carried
options.C: Number of wagons multiplied by number of days detained
options.D: Passenger-carrying capacity multiplied by train kilometres

e: NTKM is the net (paying) load of goods traffic multiplied by distance carried. It is the basic output unit of goods services, and freight unit cost is expressed per NTKM.

q: In railway accounts language, 'foreign' traffic primarily means traffic of which kind?

options.A: Traffic to a foreign country only
options.C: Traffic to, from or via another railway, as opposed to local traffic on the home railway

e: 'Foreign' traffic means inter-railway traffic - traffic to, from or via another railway. It does not primarily mean traffic to a foreign country.

q: Which suspense head is operated for inter-railway transfer transactions?

options.A: Transfer Railways
options.C: Traffic Suspense

e: Inter-railway transactions are first taken under 'Transfer Railways' and cleared when the respondent railway accepts and adjusts them. Transfer Divisional is for intra-railway transfers.

q: For which movement are no NTKMs calculated?

options.A: Loaded goods trains on the run
options.C: Goods traffic carried over the home railway

e: No NTKMs are calculated for shunting, because NTKM measures line-haul output, not every movement a vehicle makes.

q: A goods consignment is booked at a through freight of Rs. 90,000. Terminal charges are Rs. 10,000 and transhipment charges are Rs. 5,000. The distances carried are: Railway X - 200 km, Railway Y - 300 km, Railway Z - 250 km. What is the line-haul share of Railway Y?
e: Terminals and transhipment come out first: 90,000 - 10,000 - 5,000 = 75,000. Railway Y's share = 75,000 x 300 / 750 = Rs. 30,000.

q: A through passenger fare of Rs. 12,000 is to be apportioned among three railways over which the passenger travels 200 km, 300 km and 500 km respectively. What is the share of the second railway (300 km)?
e: Passenger through revenue is divided by kilometres travelled. Total distance is 1,000 km, so the second railway gets 12,000 x 300 / 1,000 = Rs. 3,600.

q: The line-haul element of a through goods freight, after deducting terminal and transhipment charges, is Rs. 1,80,000. The consignment is carried 450 km on Railway P, 350 km on Railway Q and 200 km on Railway R. What is the share of Railway P?
e: Total distance is 1,000 km. Railway P's share = 1,80,000 x 450 / 1,000 = Rs. 81,000.

q: A through goods freight is Rs. 2,20,000, out of which terminal charges of Rs. 20,000 are taken out before apportionment. The balance is carried 600 km on one railway and 400 km on another. What is the share of the railway that carried it for 400 km?
e: Balance for distance apportionment = 2,20,000 - 20,000 = 2,00,000. Share for 400 km = 2,00,000 x 400 / 1,000 = Rs. 80,000.

q: A through coaching fare of Rs. 9,600 is apportioned over distances of 120 km, 180 km and 300 km. What is the share corresponding to the longest distance of 300 km?
e: Total distance is 600 km. Share for 300 km = 9,600 x 300 / 600 = Rs. 4,800.

q: The line-haul earnings of a through movement amount to Rs. 5,00,000. Railway A carries the traffic for 250 km and Railway B for 750 km. What is the apportioned share of Railway B?
e: Total distance is 1,000 km. Railway B's share = 5,00,000 x 750 / 1,000 = Rs. 3,75,000.

q: A goods consignment is booked at a through freight of Rs. 1,50,000. Terminal charges are Rs. 18,000 and transhipment charges are Rs. 12,000. The distances carried are 300 km, 300 km and 600 km. What is the line-haul share of the railway that carried it for 600 km?
A through passenger fare of Rs. 45,000 is to be divided among railways over which the passenger travels 900 km, 600 km and 500 km. What is the share for the 500 km portion?
e: Total distance is 2,000 km. Share for 500 km = 45,000 x 500 / 2,000 = Rs. 11,250.

q: Which one of the following statements about apportionment is NOT correct?

options.A: Only through traffic needs apportionment
options.B: The originating railway retains the entire through-traffic earnings it collects
options.C: Local traffic wholly within one railway needs no apportionment
options.D: Apportionment gives each railway the share it earned, not merely the share it collected

e: The originating / collecting railway does not retain the entire through-traffic earnings. The amount is divided among all railways concerned, normally by distance.

q: Which one of the following statements about IRFA is NOT correct?

options.A: IRFA stands for Inter-Railway Financial Adjustments
options.B: IRFA transactions are settled in cash between railways
options.C: A book adjustment through Transfer Railways is also an IRFA transaction
options.D: No IRFA is raised for reservation charges

e: A book adjustment through Transfer Railways is a transfer transaction, not IRFA. IRFA is settlement in cash by financial adjustment.

q: Which one of the following statements about the Traffic Book is NOT correct?

options.A: Part A of the Traffic Book carries the net results of apportionment
options.B: Part B of the Traffic Book carries the net results of apportionment
options.C: Part C of the Traffic Book carries the Traffic Account proper
options.D: The Traffic Book includes coaching, goods, sundry and other coaching earnings

e: Part A deals with station accounts. The net results of apportionment are carried in Part B, so statement A is not correct.

q: Which one of the following statements about terminal and line-haul components is NOT correct?

options.A: Terminal expenses arise at the booking, loading, unloading and delivery points
options.B: Line-haul expenses arise on the run and grow broadly with distance
options.C: Terminal charges are taken out before the balance is apportioned by distance
options.D: Terminal expenses increase in direct proportion to the lead of the traffic

e: Terminal expenses are not affected by the lead of the traffic - loading a wagon costs the same whether it travels 50 km or 1,500 km. Statement D is therefore not correct.

q: Which one of the following statements about Transfer Railways is NOT correct?

options.A: At the year-end, a Transfer Railways balance is closed to Balance like every other suspense head
options.B: Balances under Transfer Railways should be brought to nil by the end of the year
options.C: A lingering Transfer Railways balance represents unadjusted transactions
options.D: A Transfer Certificate is the advice by which a transfer debit or credit is intimated to another railway

e: Transfer Railways is the exception: its year-end balance is closed to Miscellaneous Government Account/Revenue, whereas other suspense heads are closed to Balance.

q: Which one of the following statements about Government (defence) traffic is NOT correct?

options.A: Such traffic may be booked on credit notes / warrants issued by the department
options.B: The charges are taken under Traffic Suspense as demands recoverable
options.C: Such traffic is free traffic and no amount is recovered from the department
options.D: Clearance is effected by raising bills and recovering the amounts

e: Government traffic booked on credit notes is not free traffic. The charges are billed on the departments concerned and recovered from them.

q:
Assertion (A): Apportionment of passenger revenue relating to through traffic is done in proportion to the kilometres travelled on each railway.
Reason (R): Distance is the measure of the service rendered by each railway in carrying the through traffic.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

e: Both are true, and the reason explains the assertion: earnings are divided by distance because distance measures the carriage service each railway rendered.

q:
Assertion (A): IRFA transactions are settled by book debit and credit through the head 'Transfer Railways'.
Reason (R): Transfer transactions between railways are settled by debit and credit in the books through the head 'Transfer Railways'.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: A is true but R is false
options.C: Both A and R are false
options.D: A is false but R is true

e: The assertion is false: IRFA is settlement in cash by financial adjustment. The reason is true for transfer transactions, which are settled by book adjustment through Transfer Railways.
